learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of elementary algebraic structures, matrices and their operations.
Knowledge of linear spaces and their properties.
Knowledge of linear transformations and related theorems.
Knowledge of algorithms for solving possible linear systems.
Knowledge of conditions of diagonalizability of a matrix.
Knowledge of scalar product and Euclidean linear spaces.
Knowledge of Euclidean spaces; parallelism, orthogonality and Euclidean distance between subspaces (particularly in dimension two three).
Knowledge of the theory of conics.
Ability to calculate the determinant and rank of a matrix.
Ability to discuss and solve linear systems.
Ability to determine the basis and dimension of a linear space.
Ability to determine kernel and image of a linear transformation, checking injectivity and / or surjectivity.
Ability to calculate the eigenvalues and discuss diagonalizability of a matrix.
Ability to construct orthonormal bases in an Euclidean linear space.
Ability to determine the orthogonal complement of a given Euclidean subspace.
Ability to represent Euclidean subspaces via cartesian and parametric form.
Ability to establish the mutual position between Euclidean subspaces and calculate the distance.
Ability to classify conics of the Euclidean plane and determine the basic elements.
Attitude towards a methodological approach that leads to verify the claims and methods presented through rigorous arguments.
Ability to self-assessment of their skills and abilities.
Ability to deal with a dialectical discourse in a timely and consistent way, arguing with precision.
Acquisition of mathematical knowledge as its assets and redeem them at any other time of their cultural journey.
Attitude towards a methodological approach that leads to an improvement in the method of study leading to deepening learning capacity.

syllabus_topics: Elementary algebraic structures
Groups, rings, fields, algebras
Matrices
Operations on matrices
Determinant of a square matrix; properties of the determinant and methods of calculations of the determinant
Inverse matrix
Vector spaces
Linear combinations; systems of generators; bases and dimension
Linear transformations and their properties
Matrices associated to a linear transformation
Rank of a matrix; algorithms for the computation of the rank
Parametric and Cartesian representation of vector subspaces
Linear systems Discussion of a linear system; structure of the space of solutions of a compatible linear system
Cramer systems
Algorithms for the solution of compatible linear systems
Canonical forms of matrices Similarity of matrices; diagonalization problems
Eigenvalues, eigenvectors and eigenspaces
Algebraic and geometric multiplicity
Spectral theorem
Euclidean vector spaces Scalar product; norm of a vector; angle between vectors and orthogonality
Orthogonal bases and orthonormal bases; Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization method
Orthogonal complement of a subspace of a Euclidean space
Euclidean geometry Coordinate system; subspaces; relative positions
Euclidean plane: representations of straight lines; parallelism and othogonality; distances; areas; plane isometries
Three-dimensional Euclidean space: representations of straight lines and planes, parallelism and othogonality; distances; areas and volumes
Projective extension of an Euclidean space
Theory of conics Homogeneous and non-homogeneous equations; related matrices
Degenerate and non-degenerate conics
Classification of non degenerate conics
Polarity
Centre of a conic and its coordinates
Diameters
Asintots
Axes and vertices
Euclidean canonical equations of conics
Characterization of equilateral hyperboles, of void ellipses, of circunferences
Focus and directrix of a non-degenerate conics
Some elements about sheaves of conics
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral test. The written test has 11 multiple-choice questions (3 points for correct, -1 for incorrect, 0 for unanswered); a score of 15 or more is required to access the oral exam. Written exemption can be obtained by passing two intermediate tests with both grades >= 12 and an arithmetic mean >= 15. If an oral test has a negative result, the validity of the written test (or exemption) is limited to one further oral test within the academic year; after two negative oral tests, the written test loses validity. The final grade is established by the examiner based on the oral test, also considering the written grade.
